Let me go through each phase of the investigation. ## Phase 0: Consume Test Evidence No test evidence provided in this case - just the component code and expected behavior description. I'll proceed with normal investigation but note when claims would be stronger with measurement. ## Phase 1: Pre-commitment Predictions Based on the component type (popover/dialog), my predictions for likely accessibility design issues: 1. Missing focus management — no focus trap, no focus return to trigger after close 2. Missing ARIA attributes — no role="dialog", aria-modal, aria-labelledby/aria-label 3. No Escape key handling — keyboard users can't dismiss the popover 4. Focus doesn't move into the popover when it opens 5. Popover content not properly associated with trigger (no aria-controls, aria-expanded) ## Phase 2: Semantic HTML Audit Let me read through the code carefully: ```jsx

``` - The trigger is a native ` {content} )} ``` **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern and WCAG 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap), when the popover is open, Tab must cycle within the popover content — focus should not escape to background page elements. Currently, pressing Tab from the last focusable element in the popover moves focus to whatever comes next on the underlying page, breaking the modal mental model entirely. **Fix**: Implement a focus trap that: - Captures all focusable elements inside the popover container - On Tab at the last focusable element, redirects focus to the first focusable element (and vice versa for Shift+Tab) - Optionally use `inert` attribute on background content or the `focus-trap-react` library **Confidence**: HIGH — directly verifiable from code absence. No trap logic exists anywhere in the component. --- ### 2. Missing focus restoration after popover closes **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:17-19` — The `closePopover` function only sets state to false, with no focus management: ```jsx const closePopover = () => { setIsOpen(false); }; ``` The `triggerRef` is declared at line 6 (`const triggerRef = useRef(null)`) but never used for focus restoration. When the Close button (or any element inside the popover) unmounts, keyboard users lose their place entirely — focus falls back to `` or wherever the browser defaults. **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern and WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order), when a dialog/popover closes, focus must return to the element that triggered it — in this case `triggerRef.current`. This is especially critical because the Close button itself unmounts, so without restoration, keyboard users are stranded with no visible focus indicator anywhere on the page. **Fix**: Add focus restoration before or after state change: ```jsx const closePopover = () => { setIsOpen(false); // Restore focus to trigger — defer if needed for React unmount timing setTimeout(() => triggerRef.current?.focus(), 0); }; ``` **Confidence**: HIGH — `triggerRef` exists but is never used for `.focus()`. The absence of restoration logic is unambiguous. --- ### 3. Missing Escape key handling to dismiss popover **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:1-45` — There are NO keyboard event handlers anywhere in the component. No `onKeyDown`, no `onKeyUp`, no `useEffect` with event listeners for Escape. The only interaction handler is `onClick={openPopover}` on line 12 and `onClick={closePopover}` on line 26. **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users, screen reader users (who rely heavily on Escape to dismiss dialogs) **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern, pressing Escape must close the dialog/popover. This is one of the most fundamental keyboard interactions for modal components — it's expected by all assistive technology users and documented in WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard). Without it, keyboard users who open the popover have no efficient way to dismiss it except Tabbing through potentially many elements to find the Close button. **Fix**: Add Escape key handling: ```jsx useEffect(() => { if (!isOpen) return; const handleKeyDown = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { closePopover(); } }; document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown); return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown); }, [isOpen]); ``` **Confidence**: HIGH — grep for `onKeyDown`, `Escape`, `keydown` in the component returns zero results. No keyboard handling exists at all. --- ### 4. Missing ARIA role="dialog" on popover container (no semantic identity) **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:23-30` — The popover content `
` has only a `className`: ```jsx
``` No `role`, no `aria-modal`, no labeling attributes. **User group impacted**: Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) pattern and WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), the popover container must have `role="dialog"` to communicate its nature as a dialog to assistive technology. Without this role, screen readers treat it as generic content — they won't announce "dialog" when focus enters it, won't switch to application or document reading mode appropriately, and users won't understand that background content is supposed to be inactive. **Fix**: Add `role="dialog"` (or `role="alertdialog"` if it's an alert-type popover) to the container div: ```jsx
``` **Confidence**: HIGH — the `
` has only `className`, no ARIA attributes whatsoever. --- ### 5. Missing aria-modal="true" on popover (background remains accessible to AT) **Evidence**: Same as finding #4 — `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:23-30`. The expected behavior section explicitly states "aria-modal announces modal behavior" but this attribute is completely absent from the code. **User group impacted**: Screen reader users **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern, when a dialog is open and focus is contained within it, `aria-modal="true"` must be set on the dialog element. This tells screen readers to restrict virtual cursor navigation to the dialog content only — background page content becomes inaccessible until the dialog closes. Without this attribute, screen reader users can navigate into the underlying page while the popover appears "open," creating a deeply confusing experience where they interact with elements that are visually obscured or inactive. **Fix**: Add `aria-modal="true"` alongside `role="dialog"`: ```jsx
``` **Confidence**: HIGH — attribute is completely absent from the JSX. The expected behavior section confirms it was intended but not implemented. --- ### 6. Missing focus movement into popover when opened (no autofocus) **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:14-15` — `openPopover()` only sets state to true: ```jsx const openPopover = () => { setIsOpen(true); }; ``` No code moves focus into the popover content. The expected behavior states "Focus moves into popover after opening" but this is not implemented. **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users, screen reader users **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern and WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order), when a dialog opens, focus must move INTO the dialog — typically to the first focusable element or the Close button. Currently, after clicking the trigger, keyboard users remain focused on the trigger button and must Tab through potentially many elements before reaching the popover content. This is especially problematic if the popover appears at a different location on screen from the trigger. **Fix**: Move focus into the popover when it opens: ```jsx useEffect(() => { if (isOpen) { // Focus first focusable element or Close button in popover const closeButton = document.querySelector('.popover-content button'); setTimeout(() => closeButton?.focus(), 0); } }, [isOpen]); ``` **Confidence**: HIGH — no focus-related code exists in `openPopover()` or anywhere else. The function only calls `setIsOpen(true)`. --- ## Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) ### 7. Missing aria-expanded on trigger button (state not communicated to AT) **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:12` — The trigger button has no state attributes: ```jsx ``` **User group impacted**: Screen reader users, keyboard-only users using screen readers **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern (which popovers commonly follow) and WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), the trigger button must have `aria-expanded` that reflects whether the popover is open (`"true"`) or closed (`"false"`). Without this attribute, screen reader users get no feedback when they click the button — they don't know if content appeared or disappeared. They might click repeatedly thinking nothing happened, or be confused about the current state of the interface. **Fix**: Add `aria-expanded` bound to the `isOpen` state: ```jsx ``` **Confidence**: HIGH — button has only `ref` and `onClick`, no ARIA attributes. --- ### 8. Missing aria-controls on trigger (no programmatic relationship) **Evidence**: Same as finding #7 — `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:12`. The trigger button doesn't reference the popover it controls via `aria-controls`. **User group impacted**: Screen reader users **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern, when a control shows/hides content, it should use `aria-controls` to establish a programmatic relationship between the trigger and the controlled element. This allows screen readers to announce "controls [popover name]" and helps users understand that interacting with this button affects specific content on the page. **Fix**: Give the popover an `id` and reference it from the trigger: ```jsx {/* In popover div */}
``` **Confidence**: HIGH — no `aria-controls` attribute present on the trigger. --- ### 9. Missing aria-labelledby or aria-label on popover (no accessible name) **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:23-30` — The popover `
` has no labeling attributes at all. It only has `className="popover-content"`. **User group impacted**: Screen reader users **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) pattern and WCAG 4.1.2, a dialog must have an accessible name so screen reader users know what the popover is about when focus enters it. This can be provided via `aria-labelledby` (referencing a visible heading/title in the popover) or `aria-label` (for cases where there's no visible title). Without this, when focus moves into the popover, screen readers announce "dialog" with no context — users don't know what purpose the popover serves until they start exploring its content. **Fix**: Add labeling: ```jsx

Popover Title

{/* or if no visible title: */} {/* aria-label="Additional information" */} ``` **Confidence**: HIGH — no labeling attributes on the popover container. --- ### 10. No inert/background content management when popover is open **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx` — When `isOpen` is true, the entire page remains interactive and accessible to assistive technology. There's no mechanism (like the `inert` attribute) applied to background content or a backdrop overlay that prevents interaction with underlying elements. **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users, screen reader users, low vision users who might accidentally click through **Expected behavior**: Per WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern and WCAG 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap), when a modal dialog is open, background content should be made non-interactive — either by applying `inert` to the rest of the page or by rendering an invisible backdrop that captures clicks. Without this, keyboard users can Tab into background elements while the popover appears "open," and screen reader virtual cursor navigation reaches behind the popover (compounded by the missing `aria-modal`). **Fix**: Either: - Apply `inert` to a wrapper around all non-popover content when open, or - Render an invisible overlay/backdrop element that captures pointer events and receives focus first ```jsx {!isOpen &&

} ``` **Confidence**: MEDIUM — This is a gap in the component's design, but it could potentially be handled by parent-level code not shown here. Still, the component itself provides no mechanism for background management. --- ## Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) ### 11. Close button label "Close" is generic without context **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyPopover.jsx:26` — `` The label "Close" doesn't indicate what specifically will be closed. While this meets minimum requirements, a more descriptive label like "Close [popover purpose]" would improve clarity for screen reader users navigating by button labels. However, since the popover should have an accessible name (finding #9), and the Close button is contextually within that dialog, this is acceptable once labeling is added. **WCAG**: 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) — "Close" in context of a dialog is generally sufficient as users understand they're closing the current dialog. --- ## What's Missing (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions) 1. **Missing focus movement into popover on open** — No code moves focus from trigger to first focusable element inside popover when it opens 2. **Missing Escape key handler** — No keyboard event listeners for dismissing the popover with Escape 3. **Missing focus trap implementation** — Tab can escape the popover boundary to background content 4. **Missing focus restoration on close** — `triggerRef` is declared but never used; focus is lost when Close button unmounts 5. **Missing aria-modal="true"** — Screen reader virtual cursor can navigate behind the popover while it's "open" 6. **Missing role="dialog"** — Popover has no semantic identity as a dialog to assistive technology 7. **Missing aria-expanded on trigger** — State change (open/close) is invisible to screen readers 8. **Missing aria-controls on trigger** — No programmatic relationship between button and popover content 9. **Missing aria-labelledby/aria-label on popover** — Screen reader users get no title/context when entering the dialog 10. **No inert/background management** — Background page remains fully interactive while popover is open 11. **No keyboard event handling at all** — Component only handles `onClick`; no `onKeyDown`/`onKeyUp` for any key interactions (Escape, arrow keys, etc.) --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes ### Screen Reader User - The popover container has NO `role="dialog"`, so it's announced as generic content — screen readers won't switch to dialog mode or announce "dialog" when focus enters. - No `aria-modal="true"` means the virtual cursor can navigate into background page content while the popover appears open, creating a deeply confusing experience where users interact with visually obscured elements. - The trigger button has no `aria-expanded`, so clicking it produces zero screen reader feedback — users don't know if content appeared or disappeared. - No `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` on the popover means when focus does enter (if manually tabbed to), screen readers announce "dialog" with no context about what it's for. - The Close button label "Close" is generic but acceptable in dialog context once proper labeling exists. ### Keyboard-Only User - **No Escape key handling** — Cannot dismiss the popover with the standard keyboard shortcut; must Tab through potentially many elements to find and activate the Close button. - **Focus doesn't move into popover on open** — After clicking trigger, focus stays on the trigger button; user must Tab forward (possibly past many page elements) to reach popover content. - **No focus trap** — Pressing Tab from the last focusable element in the popover moves focus to background page elements, allowing interaction with "inactive" content behind the popover. - **Focus lost after close** — When Close button is clicked and unmounts (since `isOpen` becomes false), there's no code to restore focus to the trigger;
